inDevelopment.meta: Recruiting · n=150 · 11 sites · primary completion Jan 2029
inDevelopment.title: Nasal chondrocyte engineered cartilage (N-TEC) vs AMIC vs patellofemoral arthroplasty for patellofemoral osteoarthritis
inDevelopment.frame: University Hospital Basel. A sister trial (NCT06163573, n=75) compares N-TEC with PRP.
inDevelopment.forWork: Your 2026 Cartilage commentary names offloading the patellofemoral joint as a major unanswered area. This trial has no osteochondral allograft or offloading arm, which leaves that comparison open for a future study.

inDevelopment.meta: n=36 · vs abrasion chondroplasty · primary completion Dec 2027
inDevelopment.title: EB-OC engineered osteochondral graft for full-thickness chondral and osteochondral knee defects
inDevelopment.frame: Epibone, Inc. Registry lists it as not yet recruiting even though the listed start date is January 2026, so confirm status before citing.
inDevelopment.forWork: An engineered graft would remove donor and storage variability, the same variables tested in the 2025 donor-variable study. The comparator is chondroplasty, so your allograft cohorts would be the benchmark for any later head-to-head design.

inDevelopment.meta: Recruiting · n=5 · single site · started Jul 30, 2026
inDevelopment.title: Nanochon Chondrograft implant for resurfacing knee cartilage lesions
inDevelopment.frame: First-in-human safety and performance study of an off-the-shelf implant, Nanochon, Inc.
inDevelopment.forWork: Off-the-shelf implants depend on surface fit. Your topography-matching work (patient-specific guides, phone-based scanning) could be applied to measuring implant congruity.

inDevelopment.title: MOCHA: montelukast as a chondroprotective treatment after ACL reconstruction
inDevelopment.frame: Single-site placebo-controlled study (Austin Stone) in ACL and meniscus injury, aimed at post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
inDevelopment.forWork: It targets the knee environment, the other major gap in your Cartilage commentary. Your inflammatory biomarker and symptomatic-state work at chondroplasty offers a readout model for a similar trial in cartilage patients.

inDevelopment.meta: Recruiting · target n=1000 · started Sep 23, 2026 · runs to 2034
inDevelopment.title: C-SHORE: Cartilage Repair Study of Health Outcomes and Real-world Evidence
inDevelopment.frame: Industry registry (Smith & Nephew) comparing a marketed product with other surgical treatments for knee joint surface lesions.
inDevelopment.forWork: Its outcome interpretation could use your anchor-based MCID and PASS thresholds (for example, microfracture). A threshold-validation or secondary-analysis collaboration is worth exploring. Industry sponsor, so independence needs a look.

newPapers.meta: OJSM · Aug 2026 · Tabbaa, Bugbee et al.
newPapers.title: Association of Donor Characteristics and Graft Storage Time with Survivorship of Osteochondral Allograft Transplantation in the Knee
newPapers.frame: 220 patients (236 knees), mean follow-up 8.2 years. Donors over 20 years failed more (11.7% vs 3.7%, P=.039). Early-release grafts (1 to 14 days) failed more than late-release (22.7% vs 6%, P=.002). Donor BMI and sex matching had no effect.
newPapers.versus: Different on donor age and storage; similar on sex matching. Hevesi 2025 (372 patients, mean 5.4 years) found no association of donor sex, age, mismatch, or storage time with reoperation or failure.
newPapers.forWork: Your grafts were stored 14 to 28 days, so your cohort cannot test the under-14-day group where their signal sits. A reanalysis with their donor-age cutoff, and longer follow-up, would show whether the age signal appears in your data.

newPapers.meta: AJSM · Aug 2026 · Park, Hughes et al. (Pittsburgh)
newPapers.title: Meniscal Allograft Transplantation Failure Is Associated With Female Sex: A 15-Year Survival Analysis
newPapers.frame: 160 patients, median follow-up 15 years. Graft survival 84% at 10 years, 76% at 15, 69% at 20, 52% at 25. Female sex predicted failure only after adjusting for age and cartilage grade (P=.04).
newPapers.versus: Similar survival at 10 years; different on sex. Wagner 2023 (174 patients, mean 12.7 years) reported 84.5% failure-free survival at 10 years and 72.1% at 15, with no sex difference on log-rank (P=.390).
newPapers.forWork: Your sex comparison was unadjusted. Rerunning it as a Cox model adjusted for age and compartment cartilage grade would test whether the same sex signal appears in the Rush cohort.

newPapers.meta: J Clin Orthop Trauma · Jul 2026 · Khan, Enc · PROSPERO CRD420261342726
newPapers.title: Biologic augmentation in knee preservation surgery: A systematic review of procedure-specific evidence
newPapers.frame: 23 studies, only one low-risk RCT. Evidence for augmenting meniscal allograft, cartilage restoration, and osteochondral allograft was called insufficient for routine use. Authors ask for procedure-specific RCTs and standardized reporting of biologic preparation.
newPapers.versus: Consistent with your 2025 Arthroscopy BMAC RCT in osteochondral allograft (n=36; reoperation 5.3% vs 35.3%, P=.02; no PROM difference). Not confirmed whether it was among the 23 studies. PMID for your trial is not yet in the manifest; verify before citing.
newPapers.forWork: The review describes the gap your RCT begins to fill. A larger multicenter trial with reported BMAC cell content (your 2023 ASMAR MSC concentration paper) matches what they ask for.

newPapers.meta: Osteoarthr Cartil Open · Jun 2026 · Scheepmaker, Saris, Korpershoek (Mayo)
newPapers.title: Arthroscopically and manually minced cartilage demonstrates lower cell viability and lower proteoglycan deposition compared to isolated chondrons and chondrocytes
newPapers.frame: Laboratory study using fresh human allograft cartilage, 28 days. Viability: chondrons 93.7%, chondrocytes 94%, manual mincing 79.8%, arthroscopic mincing 56.6%. Clinical mince samples varied more than 10-fold in cellularity.
newPapers.versus: Similar direction to your work showing that graft handling lowers chondrocyte viability (reaming; irrigation temperature and reamer speed). Different tissue and model, so a parallel, not a replication.
newPapers.forWork: Your viability methods could be applied to minced and particulated cartilage, adding irrigation and temperature variables that they did not test.

newPapers.meta: Biomech Model Mechanobiol · Sep 2026 · Lamberty, Coleman (Michigan)
newPapers.title: Combined cartilage thickness and mechanical property mismatch drives local strain amplification at the patellar osteochondral allograft interface
newPapers.frame: Idealized finite element model, donor-to-recipient thickness ratios 0.33 to 3.25. Interface strain rose with thickness disparity; functionally graded stiffness lowered it. No patient data.
newPapers.versus: Different variable. Your matching work addresses surface topography (overlapping vs oblong grafts; patient-specific guides). They add thickness and stiffness as a second matching dimension.
newPapers.forWork: Thickness could be added to your topography pipeline. Their authors call for experimental and patient-specific models, which your scan-based cohorts could supply.

alsoNoted.text: Mowers et al., Arthroscopy 2026: systematic review of 973 patients found no consistent effect of donor-recipient sex mismatch on knee OCA outcomes, with bipolar grafts the best predictor of failure. Fits your 2025 donor-variable and sex-based outcome papers.
Yu et al., J ISAKOS 2026: meta-analysis of MAT at 10 years or more, pooled failure 31%, arthroplasty conversion 17%. A benchmark for your 10-year series (23% failure, 15% conversion).
